purpose.summary: Initialize the bounded optional regtest upstream service off the native initialization thread, retain the indexed old branch across honest native progress, and join startup before native teardown.
scope: Signed local review parent only, not assumed public main. Retained stop/reopen timeout remains unresolved and blocks PR readiness.
Own asynchronous import/mempool waiting, index startup and HTTP lifetime; do not hold AppInitMain on optional DB/disk work.
Seed the checked indexed old branch from the private owned graph before live transition, then reuse existing captured upstream disconnect/connect writers for progress or reorg.
Preserve strict historical fixture startup and unchanged source/epoch HTTP admission; busy or unpublished views remain 503.
Treat native startup shutdown as joined cancellation, preserve the bound root without a false failed marker, and require real upstream reopen/resync.
Bind five exact fresh-process native cases and retain real-daemon crash, default-OFF, scope-refusal and failed-root controls.
exclusions: No consensus, validation, mempool policy, activation, dependency, default, upstream indexing/token algorithm or operator configuration change.
No HTTP read-gate bypass, public listener, plugin activation, detach, fake shutdown timeout, automatic database wipe or identity rewrite.
No incoming evidence, private history, operator data, server access, deployment, cutover, release, desktop integration or proof promotion.

commands: Build the independent compiled-out profile with all upstream/plugin/observer flags OFF; execute the existing native zero-subsidy mining and positive-stop smoke.
expected_results: Native mining and shutdown work without linking Rust/Chronik; no Chronik state or external peer connection is created.

commands: Build separate archival and plugin profiles with BUILD_CHRONIK_UPSTREAM_REGTEST=OFF; run unchanged exact native selections and dormant daemon controls. Keep the enabled daemon build independent.
expected_results: No Python plugin implementation is selected; setup refuses before plugin files or state are created. Linking upstream alone starts no daemon index or listener.

commands: Build the existing regtest profile, plugins/Qt/observer OFF. Run regtest_service.py --repetitions 3 with the exact five startup cases 7/5/6/9/9, two lease cases9/6, shutdown case9, and actual daemon lifecycle. Retain all inherited matrices without changing60-second limits.
expected_results: Native import waiting and index I/O do not block initialization; accepted native progress/reorg catches up through the real upstream indexer, cancellation preserves reopen, and joined Stop precedes native resource teardown.

scenarios.command: Run the five exact startup cases in fresh native processes plus the existing real-daemon lifecycle, lease and shutdown witnesses. Keep inherited observer/full-window scenarios separate, not daemon readiness evidence.
expected_results: Three repetitions: 18 fresh daemon processes and 24 native processes, including15 startup processes with36 assertions per repetition, 6 lease processes and3 shutdown processes.

Import wait is off the calling thread, native mining progresses while initialization is latched, Stop joins admitted startup, and a reorg during private owned resync reaches the correct current tip without quarantine.
No false failed marker on native startup cancellation; actual upstream reopen succeeds. Existing source/epoch read gate, no-wipe policy, identity authority and standalone consensus are preserved.
failure_conditions: Wrong exact case/assertion selection, stale or changed source/view, mismatched plugin accepted, identity rewritten, disabled guard bypass, failed root adopted, native authority effect, skip, timeout, nonzero exit, instability or incomplete cleanup.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run feature_chronik_token_http.py: extend to height 290 in bounded batches, disconnect below the retained projection anchor, reconsider, verify mismatched restart leaves HTTP disabled, then explicitly full-reindex. Separately exercise upstream retained-anchor and source-generation contradictions; the fixture observer closes while native progress continues.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Both known and unknown token/transaction IDs return protobuf 503 after observer closure, never stale 200 or misleading 404.

Node RPC and chain selection continue; reconsider does not reopen observation. A persistent-tip mismatch disables HTTP on restart and logs recovery=reindex. Explicit full reindex restores canonical token metadata and byte-identical confirmed transaction output.
failure_conditions: Any accepted response after irreversible closure, missing-ID 404 from a degraded view, HTTP serving from a mismatched restarted runtime, missing mismatch diagnostic, failed canonical reindex recovery, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: The retained stop/reopen60-second timeout remains unexplained and blocks PR readiness. Targeted successes do not replace the required unchanged full matrix.
Initialization is asynchronous, but stalled storage still holds a positive shutdown join. No hard I/O latency, general service availability or full-chain performance promise.
Unpruned local regtest only: height <=2000, native index/pool <=4096, retained old/current branch window288, payload64MiB and callback queue128. Not measured RSS bounds.
Adapter identity changes are not an operator DB migration contract. Unknown/failed roots remain refused; no auto-wipe or identity rewrite.
Plugins, websocket/broadcast, public exposure, mainnet/testnet activation and production deployment remain disabled/out of scope. Full actual-daemon ALP lifecycle remains a later slice.
No incoming evidence or independent reproduction. Rust lock unchanged; system/SDK/runner inputs remain unlocked and upstream dependency alerts remain open.
counterevidence: On the final source, the real-daemon lifecycle passed three repetitions (18 daemon and24 native processes), and one complete inherited matrix passed45 cases/2291 assertions. A subsequent required ten-repetition matrix passed bridge/startup/capture groups ten times and the stop/reopen group six times, then refused stop/reopen repetition7 at the unchanged60-second limit with class process-timeout. No passing report was created for that repeated matrix. The earlier single pass and targeted successes do not establish its cause or replace this failed requirement.

Earlier retained stop/reopen timeout observations remain in immutable changes0049/0050. Two local per-case progress diagnostics of the unchanged parent STOP group passed13 cases/307 assertions in34.229s and28.126s, but are not qualifying reports and do not establish the prior cause. macOS sampling yielded no usable main stack within its bounded diagnostic attempts.

Simply moving the old synchronous constructor to a thread would falsely quarantine honest tip/mempool progress and could not bind the old indexed branch. This slice explicitly retains and verifies that branch before switching to live captured reconciliation; it does not remove the source/storage fences.

Initial compilation refused a missing CXX exception conversion in the new Rust closure, then a missing test include and invalid rust::Box reset call. These were source/test corrections; no assertion, timeout, selected inherited case or cleanup requirement was weakened.

A Stop test must observe stop admission before releasing the startup latch, rather than race scheduler timing. A metadata-only stopping bit is explicit; no unsafe detach or borrowed-owner teardown is accepted.

New targeted native and real-daemon observations alone do not establish production readiness, arbitrary plugins, economically funded ALP circulation, crash/power-loss durability or unrestricted chain history.
